description: Sentiment model bake-off on the Kaggle 'Sentiment Analysis for Financial News' corpus (Malo et al. 2014). All accuracy/F1 numbers are on the identical held-out test split: 483 rows, stratified, seed 42.

results.note: bake-off winner; ships in the platform
round-1 winner before the finance-domain bake-off round
no gain: base already trained on this corpus
newer architecture, no gain on this corpus

results.model: Jev 1.13 (closed System One model, zero-shot via hosted API)
results.note: weak on positive class; not deployable keyless
weak financial-tone judgment; 10x slower on CPU

conclusion: FinancialBERT wins the bake-off and ships as the core scorer; the 78k-headline FNSPID corpus was re-scored and every downstream result re-verified with it (docs/evidence/event_study_real.json, rebalance_backtest_real.json). Six models evaluated on identical data. Evaluation artifacts: kaggle/ kernels, data/cache/sentiment_eval_*.json, docs/evidence/financialbert_eval.json, docs/evidence/laya_spike.json, docs/evidence/jev_spike.json.
caveat: The finance-domain pretraining gap (96.7% vs 89.4%) is well outside noise (483 rows, stderr ~1.4pp); differences among the FinBERT variants are not.
